intro: Data in Thailand is cheap with strong coverage in cities and the main tourist islands. The only real question is whether to set up an eSIM before you fly or grab a tourist SIM at the airport. Here is the clear comparison.

blocks.html: Short answer: If your phone supports eSIM, buying a data plan online before you fly is the easiest — it activates the moment you land, with no queue. If you prefer a physical SIM or your phone has no eSIM, grab a tourist SIM at an airport counter (AIS, TrueMove H, dtac); it is simple and inexpensive.

blocks.html: The three main networks are AIS, TrueMove H and dtac. All three cover big cities and the main tourist islands well. AIS is often praised for reach in remote areas, but in cities any of the three is fine — pick whichever plan offers the best value when you travel.

blocks.title: Check eSIM support first
blocks.html: Not every phone supports eSIM. Most iPhones from the XS onward and recent flagship Android phones do, and the phone must be carrier-unlocked. Search your model plus the word eSIM before buying.

faq.q: Is the internet in Thailand fast?
faq.a: Yes — fast and cheap in major cities and main tourist islands, with widespread 4G and 5G in many areas. On small remote islands or in the mountains the signal can weaken.

faq.q: Is an eSIM better than an airport SIM?
faq.a: It is more convenient — set up before you fly and online the moment you land — but you need an eSIM-capable, unlocked phone. If you want a Thai number for calls, or your phone has no eSIM, an airport SIM is the better fit.

faq.q: Do I need to register the SIM?
faq.a: SIMs in Thailand must be registered to your passport; airport or network shops handle this for you at purchase. Just bring your passport.
